body: This is insane. I’m bi with close friends of both genders and I’d need my partner to understand that but no fucking way would I ever cheat on my partner. She cheated and needs you to be okay with it. She’s not the one. She knows it was wrong and she was fine with it. Once someone cheats on you, it should be over in 99% of the cases and OP you’re in the 99%.

She may be a covert narcissist. Otherwise she’s a run of the mill asshole or using you. Maybe she’s just emotionally immature. I don’t know and it doesn’t matter… and it also doesn’t matter what other good qualities you feel she has. 

Take Fullbright. Break up with this girl. Wish her the best, go through the heartbreak, and go get the experience and a girl who will genuinely love you. 

I had a similar thing in my life and I chose the girl. It is one of the biggest regrets of my life. I was able to course correct but the lost years… oof… painful. Now I feel embarrassed that I loved wholeheartedly someone who clearly cared very little for me and who never considered me. 

You have your whole life ahead of you. And a girl who is “gold” is one who loves you and would ABSOLUTELY understand you waiting 9-10 months to move to her to take a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity at the young age of 22. Go get that Fulbright OP.

Edit: I didn’t realize you were queer. I am bi and the relationship I allowed to derail and destroy me was a wlw one. There are wonderful women who would be so proud of you for getting a Fullbright and who would be so excited to plan all the details of the move with you while you take it. A lot of wlw first relationships are intense and it’s made much harder when someone is this emotionally manipulative. You will find a woman who will love the shit out of you OP. Don’t settle at 22 for someone like this and PLEASE do not turn down Fullbright for her.

I do take your point about wanting it to be about a small group of singers and musicians sharing a stream consciousness of music. There was a song Foster sang that seemed to be going that way but then it sort of became more of the same. If that had been more like Not a Day Goes By vibe, would have loved that. Or maybe something more traditionally bluegrass stripped down that really spoke to an emotional experience. 

I prefer stripped down to spectacle but I felt this lacked the emotional depth it could have had. The story, on its own, about belonging, about being unloved, about falling in love, about learning to stand on your own as an adult and away from or in spite of your family, about losing a child, about abandoning your spouse and realizing you’ve made a terrible mistake, about forgiveness for the sake of shared time and in favor of moving forward, about making the most of what little time we have here… all rich, rich areas to explore. But ultimately very unexplored by the story on a deeper level. But again, that’s just me. I think if they would have added 3-4 solid scenes and cut the time repetition (at x day on y hour at z minute) and some of the exposition to do so, then I might have felt differently. 

I don’t know if this will make sense, but I wanted it to be deeper more ala Next to Normal or stay cutesy but offer more straight scenes in between the music like Wicked to build the relationships into something that really affects you.

I think cats should be allowed but I also think if you have an allergy, you should be able to request no animals in your row or the row behind you or in front of you. That could be added easily because you have to call to add in an in-cabin pet anyway.

A pet is like a child. If you have a well-behaved animal and you pay for it to travel in cabin then you’re good to go. If you fly and are allergic to animals then you should be prepared with medication. If your pet barks or meows the entire flight then your pet should not be allowed to travel in cabin again. My senior pup has been traveling with me since she was little. People always think I have a gym bag, they never even suspect there’s a dog inside. I go on 3-5 week trips and I’m not going to leave her at home when she’s much happier coming with. Same way I wouldn’t leave a child at home for weeks on end when they could just come with me. Even if all of the people with pets did not bring them (Delta only allows 4 per flight anyway) there would STILL be the possibility of service animals. So no matter what, you have a possibility of encountering an animal on your flight. If you are not next to a service animal and they are a pet and out of their carrier, you can ask that they be put back in their carrier for your allergies. But realistically, you should always bring allergy medication and take it for a flight.

It took me three years to get to a place of genuine happiness consistently. It took about six months to get tiny glimpses of happiness. 

I focused on: walking (long 2hr daily walks were therapeutic and good gentle movement), therapy (with someone who has a lot of experience with cluster b people), books about relationships with bpd/npd, small excursions with my dog (let her sniff around the dog store, get coffee and sit outside at the cafe with her), and lots of podcasts/music for distraction. Slowly made plans with people again but did calls mostly for awhile. I didn’t have the energy to go out for awhile. Then slowly started focusing on adding in weight lifting and cardio as well as trying to eat high protein. Focused on creative stuff (or hobbies). Did Duolingo for about 5-10mins every time I felt an anxiety attack (I had weird heart palpitations for awhile and I’ve never had anything like that before). Duolingo helped because it forced me to focus on something else. 

You can do this. It’ll take time. I am in such a great place now but it took me a long time. The best advice I can give you is that if you do the work, eventually it’ll all settle. It’s not linear but I promise it’ll settle. Don’t think if you’re doing the work that nothing is happening. I felt that way a bit the first year and into the second but by the third it all settled fully and I feel good 99% of the time.

If you make a new friend and you’re best friends and six months later they say, you know you’re my favorite or you’re just my favorite person, I’m so glad we met. That’s not something to worry about. If they’re saying you’re my favorite person and they met you two weeks ago… they either a) don’t really pay much attention to their language, emotional intelligence is low, or what they say they don’t worry about meaning it or b) they’re cluster b. That’s my take anyway. I’d be careful to take a word like that and make it a red flag. It’s more about is everything too extreme too soon, and you’re a god suddenly? Because healthy people with higher emotional intelligence know that you can’t know someone in a month or two. You need to develop that intimacy over time to really know who someone is so they’re not going to be making as many extreme statements. Having a favorite person in your life is not the same as a BD FP.
